Overview

zarrcurator analyzes Zarr stores for completeness and sizing, supports visualization, and can package selected content into tar archives for downstream archival workflows.

Build Documentation

From the repository root:

sphinx-build -b html docs docs/_build/html
sphinx-build -b pdf docs docs/_build/pdf

Generated artifacts:

  • HTML index: docs/_build/html/index.html

  • PDF: docs/_build/pdf/zarrcurator.pdf

Regenerate API Docstring Page

python scripts/generate_api_docstrings.py

Object Store Credentials

zarrcurator supports anonymous-first access for supported S3 endpoints. If a store is private, you can set credentials explicitly via utility APIs.

Preferred helper:

import zarrcurator

zarrcurator.setObjectStoreCredentials(
	accessKey="AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID",  # or literal access key value
	secretKey="AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY",  # or literal secret value
)

Per-call credentials are also accepted by store-facing utilities such as:

  • diagnoseStore(…, accessKey=…, secretKey=…)

  • findMissingChunksInStore(…, accessKey=…, secretKey=…)

  • displayStoreSunburst(…, accessKey=…, secretKey=…)

The generated .check report from findMissingChunksInStore includes per-variable missing, zero_size, corrupt, and unexpected chunk lists.

Chunk keys are recognised for zarr v2 (0.1, 0/1) and zarr v3 (c/0/1, c.0.1, and the v2-style encoding without the c prefix). In the report, zero_size and corrupt list the chunk keys as found in the store, while missing lists dot-separated chunk coordinates (e.g. 0.0.1) regardless of layout. A zero-size chunk cannot be read, so it is also listed under corrupt. All arrays are checked, including those in nested groups; sharded arrays are checked by shard. See Store Layouts for zarr v2/v3, nested groups (DataTree) and sharding, and Known Issues and Limitations.

Synthetic Test Stores

python -m zarrcurator.synthetic_store creates small stores with injected anomalies for end-to-end checks:

  • --zarr-formats 2,3 selects the formats and --separators .,/ the chunk key separators; without --separators each format uses its default (v2 ., v3 /).

  • --shards 4,4,8 also creates the zarr v3 stores with sharded data variables; the shard shape must be a multiple of the chunk shape 2,4,4.

  • --layouts flat,tree also creates stores with nested groups: time in the root group, lat, lon, temp and humidity in /atmos, and salinity in /atmos/ocean, which uses the coordinates of the groups above it.

The variant is tagged in the store name, only where it differs from the default, e.g. syntheticexp_P1D_000_z2slash.zarr or syntheticexp_P1D_000_z3shardtree.zarr. The manifest.json written next to the stores records each store’s variant, the array the anomalies are injected into (temp, or atmos/ocean/salinity in a tree) and the anomalies, with paths relative to its own directory.

dispatchStoreToTarStores(...) supports both local-disk and object-store Zarr backends. It first checks that the store opens with xarray (xarray.open_datatree) and raises a ValueError otherwise, before any diagnosis or tarball is made.
